newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt ignores PPI, tracks Germany.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt ignores PPI, tracks Germany.

text.p: The Swedish debt market ignored an unexpected fall in June PPI and instead tracked higher German yields. The crown was softer against the mark after profit-taking in New York last night.
"PPI came out lower than expected but previous CPI's and PPI's have exceeded expectations. This is just a sort of normalisation", one dealer said.

PPI fell by 0.1 percent in June while the market expected a rise of 0.3 percent. Profit-taking in New York made the crown soften against the mark but dealers said the positive trend had not been broken.
"What happened last night seems to have spilled over into today's trade but the positive trend is not broken", said one dealer. He saw 4.25 crowns to the mark next week.

"I don't see the dollar regaining strength and I have seen a lot of foreign interests in the crown", he continued. The crown is expected to trade between 4.29 and 4.32 crowns to the mark for the rest of the day.

The six-month T-bill rose three basis points to 4.32 percent and the ten year bond yield rose seven points to 6.46 percent. The crown softened to 4.3090 crowns against the mark versus 4.2885 crowns on Thursday. -- Stockholm newsroom +46 -8-700 1017
